caption.text: An incense vessel takes the form of a mythical beast. Made in Qianlong-period China, its gilt bronze and gemstone inlays join practical containment with an imagined animal body. The object asks an animal shape to perform a task: to hold incense as well as attract the eye.

proposals.reason: The exact accession is a covered censer, not an animal sculpture assigned a new modern function. Qianlong-period China, gilt bronze and gemstone inlays are museum facts.

caption.text: A brown patina shapes the play of color across this bronze. Pompon’s small Cosette carries the heavy pail described by Victor Hugo. The museum dates this statuette to 1888 and attributes its casting to Siot-Decauville. Material and finish help give weight to the figure’s task.

proposals.reason: An exact brown-patinated bronze object addresses surface/material; do not borrow the much larger plaster version’s height or identity.

caption.text: Two adult lions and a cub support a surface made for the sleeper’s head. This Liao-dynasty ceramic pillow joins use, ornament and protection: Cleveland connects the lions with warding off evil spirits during sleep. The animals’ strength has a domestic purpose, protecting a resting human body.

proposals.reason: An animal form literally supports sleep; the specific protective association is museum-supported rather than treated as universal animal symbolism.

caption.text: Alexander’s image outlived his rule. This posthumous head gives him an upward gaze, swept-back hair and idealized youthful features. Probably carved in Ptolemaic Egypt, it belongs to the continued veneration of a ruler worshiped as a god after his death. Authority persists through a carefully maintained likeness.

proposals.reason: Distinct from existing Trajan: posthumous idealization and divine reception make political presence survive the ruler. Egypt remains probable, not certain.

caption.text: A new emperor emerged from the portrait of a condemned predecessor. This marble head was recut from Nero into Vespasian after Nero’s condemnation of memory. Traces of the earlier hairstyle and facial features remain. Political authority was changed by removing stone, while the same material carried both identities.

proposals.reason: A concrete example of authority materially rewritten, avoiding another generic emperor portrait and preserving the exact recut-object history.

caption.text: A bowl becomes a painted devotional image. Saint Francis receiving the stigmata occupies the curved surface of this maiolica vessel, made in Deruta in 1531. Its tin glaze carries the narrative across an object with depth and a rim, bringing the image into the shape of a usable container.

proposals.reason: Adds a specific painted and glazed surface to an exhibition already comparing incision/relief/metalwork; subject, date, place and technique are museum-supported.

caption.text: Pursuit meets transformation as Daphne becomes a tree. Soldani’s terracotta group, made in Florence around 1700, draws on Bernini’s earlier marble composition. The bodies’ different directions make a fixed object describe an unfolding event. The urgency of escape gives the figures’ apparent closeness its tension.

proposals.reason: Apollo and Daphne offers pursuit/transformation and directional composition, with exact Soldani authorship and Bernini inspiration distinct. Native QA must confirm all supports/limbs/foliage survive.
